# `k.test`

Import each declaration by name, for example `import k.test.Element`.

| Declaration | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`Element`](#element) | A handle to the elements a query matched. |
| [`InlineJobQueue`](#inlinejobqueue) | A [`JobQueue`](k-server.md#jobqueue) for tests that runs each job when the enqueuing app-level transaction commits, or at once outside one: `use InlineJobQueue for JobQueue`. |
| [`Key`](#key) | A key for [`Element.press`](#element). |
| [`MemoryStorage`](#memorystorage) | The default [`LocalStorage`](k-storage.md#localstorage) in `k test`: empty for every test, able to simulate failures (`docs/design/36-local-storage.md`). |
| [`RecordingEmailProvider`](#recordingemailprovider) | The default [`EmailProvider`](k-server.md#emailprovider) in `k test`: it keeps sent messages. |
| [`RecordingJobQueue`](#recordingjobqueue) | The default [`JobQueue`](k-server.md#jobqueue) in `k test`: it stores jobs without running them; [`InlineJobQueue`](#inlinejobqueue) runs them instead. |
| [`render`](#render) | Mounts `view` in the test's browser container (`docs/design/21-testing.md`, "Rendering and querying"). |
| [`Screen`](#screen) | A rendered view, returned by `render(_:)`. |
| [`TestClient`](#testclient) | Sends requests through the whole server stack in-process: routing, guards, server rendering and endpoint pages (`docs/design/21-testing.md`, "HTTP-level tests"). |
| [`TestClipboard`](#testclipboard) | The default [`Clipboard`](k-device.md#clipboard) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Clipboard"): a clipboard in memory, empty for every test, never the machine's. |
| [`TestClock`](#testclock) | Virtual time for tests, the default [`Clock`](k-time.md#clock) in `k test` (`docs/design/35-time.md`, "Testing with TestClock"). |
| [`TestConnectivity`](#testconnectivity) | The default [`Connectivity`](k-device.md#connectivity) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Connectivity"): the device is online until `goOffline()`. |
| [`TestFiles`](#testfiles) | The default [`Files`](k-device.md#files) in `k test` (`docs/design/42-files.md`): no picker opens. |
| [`TestGeolocation`](#testgeolocation) | The default [`Geolocation`](k-device.md#geolocation) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Geolocation"): no prompt opens and the machine's position is never read. |
| [`TestHttpClient`](#testhttpclient) | The default [`HttpClient`](k-http.md#httpclient) in `k test`: it answers only requests it has a canned response for, and fails the test on any other. |
| [`TestPageVisibility`](#testpagevisibility) | The default [`PageVisibility`](k-device.md#pagevisibility) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Page visibility"): the page is visible until `hide()`. |
| [`TestPreferences`](#testpreferences) | The default [`Preferences`](k-device.md#preferences) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Preferences"): no preference is set until the test sets one. |
| [`TestRemote`](#testremote) | The `.test` binding of every `remote` rule, also when the serving app is a member of the same workspace (`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`): an in-process double of protocol `P` whose every rpc fails with `rpcFailure(.offline)` ([`k.rpc.RpcFailure.offline`](k-rpc.md#rpcfailure)), so each service's tests stay hermetic and never open a socket. |
| [`TestShare`](#testshare) | The default [`Share`](k-device.md#share) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Web Share"): no sheet opens; every share is recorded, and the user picks a target unless the test says otherwise. |
| [`TestViewport`](#testviewport) | The default [`Viewport`](k-device.md#viewport) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Viewport"): a 1280×800 viewport with a fine pointer that can hover, until the test changes one. |

## Element

```k,ignore
public class Element
```

A handle to the elements a query matched. A singular query returns a
handle even when nothing matches; an action on a handle that matches
nothing, or several elements, fails the test.

Every handle supports the queries of [`Screen`](#screen), scoped to its subtree.

**Members**

- `var exists: Bool`
  `true` if exactly one element matched.
- `var isVisible: Bool`
  `true` if it exists and is visible.
- `var isChecked: Bool`
  `true` for a checked checkbox.
- `var isPressed: Bool`
  `true` for a pressed button.
- `var isDisabled: Bool`
  `true` for a disabled control.
- `var value: String`
  The current text of a field.
- `var text: String`
  The element's text content.
- `var level: Int`
  The level of a heading, `1...6`.
- `func click()`
  Clicks the element and flushes synchronous updates.
- `func fill(_ text: String)`
  Replaces a field's value and fires input events.
- `func press(_ key: Key)`
  Presses `key` ([`Key`](#key)); [`Key.enter`](#key) in a form field submits the
  form.
- `func blur()`
  Moves the focus away from the element, firing `blur` and
  `focusout`, as leaving a form field does (it starts the field's
  `@Check` rules, `docs/design/15-forms-and-validation.md`).
- `func drag(to target: Element)`
  Drags the element onto `target` with the mouse: presses it, moves
  onto `target` and releases there (`docs/design/41-drag-and-drop.md`,
  "Tests").
- `func appear()`
  Makes the element appear in the viewport, firing its `appeared`
  event (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Element events"). The
  test DOM has no layout, so nothing appears unless a test says so.
- `func disappear()`
  Makes the element leave the viewport, firing its `disappeared`
  event.
- `func resize(width: Length, height: Length)`
  Gives the element's content box a new size, firing its `resized`
  event.
- `func heading(named name: String) -> Element`
  The heading whose accessible name is exactly `name`.
- `func link(named name: String) -> Element`
  The link whose accessible name is exactly `name`.
- `func button(named name: String) -> Element`
  The button whose accessible name is exactly `name`.
- `func text(_ text: String) -> Element`
  The element whose text is exactly `text`, after whitespace
  normalisation.
- `func text(containing text: String) -> Element`
  An element whose text contains `text`.
- `func textField(labeled label: String) -> Element`
  The text field labelled exactly `label`.
- `func passwordField(labeled label: String) -> Element`
  The password field labelled exactly `label`.
- `func textArea(labeled label: String) -> Element`
  The text area labelled exactly `label`.
- `func numberField(labeled label: String) -> Element`
  The number field labelled exactly `label`.
- `func dropdown(labeled label: String) -> Element`
  The dropdown labelled exactly `label`.
- `func checkbox(labeled label: String) -> Element`
  The checkbox labelled exactly `label`.
- `func item(containing text: String) -> Element`
  A list item whose text contains `text`.
- `func navigation(named name: String) -> Element`
  The `nav` landmark whose accessible name is exactly `name`.
- `func list() -> Element`
  Returns the only list.
- `func list(named name: String) -> Element`
  The list whose accessible name is exactly `name`.
- `func alert() -> Element`
  The only `.role(.alert)` live region.
- `func status() -> Element`
  The only `.role(.status)` live region.
- `func items() -> List<Element>`
  Returns every list item, in document order.
- `func buttons() -> List<Element>`
  Returns every button, in document order.
- `func headings() -> List<Element>`
  Returns every heading, in document order.
- `func links() -> List<Element>`
  Returns every link, in document order.

## InlineJobQueue

```k,ignore
public service InlineJobQueue implements JobQueue
```

A [`JobQueue`](k-server.md#jobqueue) for tests that runs each job when the enqueuing app-level
transaction commits, or at once outside one: `use InlineJobQueue for
JobQueue`.

**Members**

- `func enqueue<Payload>(_ kind: JobKind<Payload>, payload: Payload, delay: Duration = 0.seconds) async where Payload implements Codable`
  Runs the job at commit (or at once outside a transaction); a
  retryable failure fails the test.

## MemoryStorage

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: LocalStorage)
public service MemoryStorage implements LocalStorage
```

The default [`LocalStorage`](k-storage.md#localstorage) in `k test`: empty for every test, able to
simulate failures (`docs/design/36-local-storage.md`).

**Members**

- `func read<T>(key: StorageKey<T>) throws StorageReadError -> T? where T implements Codable`
  Reads `key` from memory, or throws the error set by
  `failReads(error:)`.
- `func write<T>(key: StorageKey<T>, value: T) throws StorageWriteError where T implements Codable`
  Writes `value` under `key` in memory, or throws the error set by
  `failWrites(error:)`.
- `func remove<T>(key: StorageKey<T>)`
  Removes `key` from memory.
- `func writeRaw(name: String, text: String)`
  Stores `text` under the key named `name` exactly as given, bypassing
  encoding, to test reading what an older version stored.
- `func failReads(error: StorageReadError)`
  Makes every following `read(key:)` throw `error`.
- `func failWrites(error: StorageWriteError)`
  Makes every following `write(key:value:)` throw `error`.
- `func stopFailing()`
  Ends both simulations (`failReads(error:)` and
  `failWrites(error:)`).

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: EmailProvider)

```

The default [`EmailProvider`](k-server.md#emailprovider) in `k test`: it keeps sent messages.

- `func send(email: Email) async throws EmailError`

## RecordingJobQueue

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: JobQueue)
public service RecordingJobQueue implements JobQueue
```

The default [`JobQueue`](k-server.md#jobqueue) in `k test`: it stores jobs without running
them; [`InlineJobQueue`](#inlinejobqueue) runs them instead.

**Members**

- `func enqueue<Payload>(_ kind: JobKind<Payload>, payload: Payload, delay: Duration = 0.seconds) async where Payload implements Codable`
  Records the job, for `payloads(of:)`.
- `func payloads<Payload>(of kind: JobKind<Payload>) -> List<Payload> where Payload implements Codable`
  Returns the payloads enqueued for `kind`, in order.

## render

```k,ignore
public func render(_ view: View) -> Screen
```

Mounts `view` in the test's browser container
(`docs/design/21-testing.md`, "Rendering and querying"). A page renders
without its layout, with its guards applied.

- Parameter view: the component or page to render, such as
  `Counter(start: 1)`.
- Returns: the [`Screen`](#screen) to query and act on.

## TestClient

```k,ignore
public service TestClient
```

Sends requests through the whole server stack in-process: routing,
guards, server rendering and endpoint pages
(`docs/design/21-testing.md`, "HTTP-level tests").

**Members**

- `func send(request: HttpRequest) async -> HttpResponse`
  Sends `request` through the server stack. Never throws.

  - Returns: the response the app produced, with any status.

## TestClipboard

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: Clipboard)
public service TestClipboard implements Clipboard
```

The default [`Clipboard`](k-device.md#clipboard) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`,
"Clipboard"): a clipboard in memory, empty for every test, never the
machine's.

**Members**

- `var text: String?`
  What the clipboard holds; `nil` until something is copied.
- `var isSupported: Bool`
  `true` unless `setSupported(_:)` said otherwise.
- `var calls: Int`
  The number of writes and reads so far, failed ones included.
- `func write(text: String) async throws ClipboardWriteError`
  Puts `text` on the clipboard, or throws the error set by
  `failWrites(error:)` (`.unsupported` after `setSupported(false)`).
- `func readText() async throws ClipboardReadError -> String?`
  Answers `text`, or throws the error set by `failReads(error:)`
  (`.unsupported` after `setSupported(false)`).
- `func set(text: String)`
  Puts `text` on the clipboard, as if another application copied it.
- `func failWrites(error: ClipboardWriteError)`
  Makes every following write throw `error`.
- `func failReads(error: ClipboardReadError)`
  Makes every following read throw `error`.
- `func setSupported(_ value: Bool)`
  Sets `isSupported`; while it is `false` every call throws
  `.unsupported`.

## TestClock

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: Clock)
public service TestClock implements Clock
```

Virtual time for tests, the default [`Clock`](k-time.md#clock) in `k test`
(`docs/design/35-time.md`, "Testing with TestClock"). It starts at
2026-01-01T12:00:00Z (UTC) unless the test sets it, and is shared by the
test's server and browser containers.

**Members**

- `var now: Date`
  The current virtual instant.
- `func every(_ interval: Duration, _ action: () -> Void) -> TimerHandle`
  Runs `action` every `interval` of virtual time.
- `func after(_ delay: Duration, _ action: () -> Void) -> TimerHandle`
  Runs `action` once after `delay` of virtual time.
- `func sleep(_ duration: Duration) async`
  Suspends until `duration` of virtual time has passed.
- `func advance(by duration: Duration)`
  Moves virtual time forward by `duration`, firing every timer and
  sleep that falls due, in order.
- `func set(now: Date)`
  Sets the virtual instant to `now`, before the code under test reads
  it.

## TestConnectivity

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: Connectivity)
public service TestConnectivity implements Connectivity
```

The default [`Connectivity`](k-device.md#connectivity) in `k test`
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Connectivity"): the device is
online until `goOffline()`. It is the one offline switch of `k test`.

**Members**

- `var isOnline: Bool`
  `true` until `goOffline()`. Reactive, like the browser's.
- `func goOffline()`
  Takes the device offline: `isOnline` turns `false`, and every rpc
  the test's browser makes fails with `rpcFailure(.offline)` until
  `goOnline()`.
- `func goOnline()`
  Brings the device back online.

## TestFiles

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: Files)
public service TestFiles implements Files
```

The default [`Files`](k-device.md#files) in `k test` (`docs/design/42-files.md`): no picker
opens. The test says what the user chooses before the code under test
asks, and reads what was saved.

**Members**

- `var saved: List<File>`
  Every file saved so far, oldest first.
- `var requests: List<List<FileType>>`
  The `types` of every `open(accepting:)` and
  `openAll(accepting:)` so far, oldest first.
- `func open(accepting types: List<FileType>) async throws FileOpenError -> File`
  Answers with the next chosen file (`choose(_:)`), or throws
  [`FileOpenError.cancelled`](k-device.md#fileopenerror) when the test chose none.
- `func openAll(accepting types: List<FileType>) async throws FileOpenError -> List<File>`
  Answers with every chosen file, or throws
  [`FileOpenError.cancelled`](k-device.md#fileopenerror) when the test chose none.
- `func save(_ file: File) throws FileSaveError`
  Records `file` in `saved`, or throws the error set by
  `failSaves(error:)`.
- `func choose(_ file: File)`
  Makes the user choose `file` at the next `open(accepting:)` or
  `openAll(accepting:)`.
- `func failOpen(error: FileOpenError)`
  Makes the next `open(accepting:)` or `openAll(accepting:)`
  throw `error`.
- `func failSaves(error: FileSaveError)`
  Makes every following `save(_:)` throw `error`.

## TestGeolocation

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: Geolocation)
public service TestGeolocation implements Geolocation
```

The default [`Geolocation`](k-device.md#geolocation) in `k test`
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Geolocation"): no prompt opens and
the machine's position is never read. The browser is capable, the
permission starts at `.prompt`, the user answers prompts with
`.granted`, and the device has no fix until `move(to:)`.

**Members**

- `var isSupported: Bool`
  `true` unless `setSupported(_:)` said otherwise.
- `var permission: PermissionState`
  `.prompt` until a prompt is answered or `setPermission(_:)`
  changes it. Reactive, like the browser's.
- `var prompts: Int`
  The number of `requestAccess()` calls that asked the user.
- `var lastAccuracy: LocationAccuracy?`
  The accuracy of the latest `currentPosition` or `watch`; `nil`
  before either.
- `func requestAccess() async -> PermissionState`
  Asks while `permission` is `.prompt`, counting it in `prompts`
  and answering what `answerPrompts(with:)` set; otherwise answers
  the permission as it is.
- `func currentPosition(accuracy: LocationAccuracy = .coarse, maximumAge: Duration = 0.seconds, timeout: Duration = 15.seconds) async throws LocationError -> Position`
  The position set by `move(to:)`, or what `failNext(error:)` set,
  `.unsupported`, `.notAsked`, `.denied`, or `.unavailable` before
  the device has moved.
- `func watch(accuracy: LocationAccuracy = .coarse) throws LocationError -> Stream<Position>`
  A stream of every position `move(to:)` sets, starting with the
  current one; it ends when the permission stops being `.granted`.
- `func move(to position: Position)`
  Moves the device: `currentPosition` answers `position`, and every
  open `watch` yields it.
- `func answerPrompts(with answer: PermissionState)`
  How the user answers the next prompts; `.granted` by default.
- `func setPermission(_ permission: PermissionState)`
  Changes `permission` as the site's settings would; anything but
  `.granted` ends every open `watch`.
- `func failNext(error: LocationError)`
  Makes the next `currentPosition` throw `error`.
- `func setSupported(_ value: Bool)`
  Sets `isSupported`; while it is `false` every call throws
  `.unsupported`.

## TestHttpClient

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: HttpClient)
public service TestHttpClient implements HttpClient
```

The default [`HttpClient`](k-http.md#httpclient) in `k test`: it answers only requests it has a
canned response for, and fails the test on any other.

**Members**

- `var requests: List<HttpRequest>`
  Every request sent so far.
- `func send(request: HttpRequest) async throws HttpError -> HttpResponse`
  Answers the canned response for the request's path, or throws the
  error set by `fail(path:error:)`; a request with nothing canned
  fails the test.
- `func respond(path: String, with response: HttpResponse)`
  Answers requests to `path` with `response`.
- `func serveJson<T>(path: String, _ value: T) where T implements Codable`
  Answers requests to `path` with `value` as JSON and status
  [`HttpStatus.ok`](k-http.md#httpstatus).
- `func serveText(path: String, _ text: String, status: HttpStatus = .ok)`
  Answers requests to `path` with `text` and `status`.
- `func fail(path: String, error: HttpError)`
  Makes requests to `path` throw `error`.

  Sets `prefersMoreContrast`.
- `func set(forcedColors value: Bool)`
  Sets `forcedColors`.

## TestRemote

```k,ignore
@ServerOnly
public struct TestRemote<P>
```

The `.test` binding of every `remote` rule, also when the serving app is
a member of the same workspace
(`docs/design/40-workspaces-and-services.md`): an in-process double of
protocol `P` whose every rpc fails with `rpcFailure(.offline)`
([`k.rpc.RpcFailure.offline`](k-rpc.md#rpcfailure)), so each service's tests stay hermetic
and never open a socket. A test that needs answers binds its own fake
with a `use` rule: `use FakePayments for Payments`.

## TestShare

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: Share)
public service TestShare implements Share
```

The default [`Share`](k-device.md#share) in `k test` (`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`,
"Web Share"): no sheet opens; every share is recorded, and the user
picks a target unless the test says otherwise.

**Members**

- `var shared: List<ShareContent>`
  Everything shared so far, oldest first.
- `var isSupported: Bool`
  `true` unless `setSupported(_:)` said otherwise.
- `func share(_ content: ShareContent) async throws ShareError`
  Records `content` in `shared`, or throws what `cancelNext()` or
  `failNext(error:)` set (`.unsupported` after
  `setSupported(false)`).
- `func cancelNext()`
  Makes the user close the next share sheet:
  [`ShareError.cancelled`](k-device.md#shareerror).
- `func failNext(error: ShareError)`
  Makes the next share throw `error`.
- `func setSupported(_ value: Bool)`
  Sets `isSupported`; while it is `false` every share throws
  `.unsupported`, and a [`k.device.ShareButton`](k-device.md#sharebutton) copies instead.

## TestViewport

```k,ignore
@TestDefault(replaces: Viewport)
public service TestViewport implements Viewport
```

The default [`Viewport`](k-device.md#viewport) in `k test`
(`docs/design/45-web-platform.md`, "Viewport"): a 1280×800 viewport
with a fine pointer that can hover, until the test changes one. Each
member is reactive, like the browser's.

**Members**

- `var size: ViewportSize?`
  1280×800 until `resize(width:height:)`.
- `var pointer: PointerKind?`
  `.fine` until `set(pointer:)`.
- `var canHover: Bool?`
  `true` until `set(canHover:)`.
- `func resize(width: Length, height: Length)`
  Resizes the viewport, as turning a phone or resizing the window
  does.
- `func set(pointer value: PointerKind)`
  Sets the primary pointer.
- `func set(canHover value: Bool)`
  Sets whether the primary pointer can hover.
